title: Moving fire survivors off FEMA interim housing
summary: Officials said two interim housing sites, including Kīlohana units, are moving from FEMA to county or Office of Recovery control while the county launches rental help for people losing FEMA lease aid, with about 1,100 people in interim housing expected near zero by 2030. A member said some Kīlohana residents did not know about the change, officials said not everyone there is eligible to stay, and a clinician said patients worry about FEMA making them leave.

timeline.text: A clinician said patients worry about FEMA making them leave at the end of the month.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: He said not everyone at Kīlohana is eligible to stay.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: He said the county is meeting with FEMA so caseworkers can meet together with Kīlohana residents.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: He said the land is also moving from HHFDC to the County of Maui.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Kīlohana temporary housing units are moving from FEMA control to county control.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A member said some people living at Kīlohana did not know the county was acquiring the units.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A FEMA sales and donations program approved just before the meeting lets FEMA transfer temporary units to the state or county.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Officials said the intent is to turn the 157 small homes into permanent housing.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: An official said about 1,100 people now in interim housing should be close to zero by 2030.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The housing director said the state plans a new notice moving one site's move-out date closer to the end of February.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Officials said the concern is what happens to households in existing programs if FEMA stops providing help.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The county is launching a rental assistance program for people who fall out of FEMA lease help.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: One interim site has 157 small homes now run and paid for by FEMA.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Two interim housing sites for disaster survivors are moving to Office of Recovery management while permanent homes are built.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said the mayor asked HIEMA to request a limited extension from FEMA.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
